children: French and German day-ahead power prices edged up on Tuesday despite a milder demand outlook in both markets, LSEG data showed, with French prices supported by low wind and extended nuclear outages, while German gains came even as wind output was forecast to rebound sharply and consumption held broadly steady.
The French baseload spot electricity contract (TRFRBD1) rose 3% to €153 ($177.63) per megawatt hour (MWh) at 0834 GMT, LSEG data showed.
"Spot prices face upward pressure from the prolonged wind lull and persistent hydro and nuclear constraints," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote in a note.

French wind output is projected to fall by 0.31 GW to 5 GW on the day ahead, while solar generation is seen up by 0.6 GW to 5.1 GW and consumption is expected to fall by 1.5 GW to 44.9 GW, LSEG data showed.
French nuclear availability fell by three percentage points to 77% of total availability.
Nuclear operator EDF issued a 24-hr strike notice from the evening of September 1.

Both the Chooz 1 and 2 reactor outages due to low river levels were moved back 4 days to September 22, operator EDF said. The reactor 2 is offline since July 10, while the reactor 1 is offline since the start of August.
The German equivalent contract (TRDEBD1) was up 0.6% to €145.90/MWh, the data showed.

German wind power generation is forecast to rise by 7.9 GW to 26.3 GW on the day ahead, while solar output is expected to fall by 3.1 GW to 11.9 GW and consumption is seen holding broadly steady at 53.8 GW, LSEG data showed.
Along the curve, the German 2027 baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) and its French equivalent (TRFRBYc1) were untraded.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was broadly stable, at €84.90 a metric ton.
